content.value_statement: Complex AI coding projects need clear coordination, memory, and review steps. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured hive mind workflows for planning and execution.
actual_capabilities: Explains queen-led coordination patterns for strategic, tactical, and adaptive project management.
Provides command examples for initializing, spawning, pausing, resuming, and monitoring hive mind sessions.
Describes consensus options including majority, weighted, and Byzantine decision workflows.
Outlines shared memory types, retrieval patterns, associations, and session checkpoint practices.
Shows integration patterns for Claude Code, SPARC workflows, repository analysis, and code review coordination.
Documents performance, troubleshooting, and configuration guidance for advanced hive mind usage.
limitations: Requires Claude Flow or compatible tooling to run the documented commands.
Does not provide executable implementation files inside this skill package.
Assumes users understand multi-agent workflows and local command execution risks.
Performance claims depend on the local project, tooling version, and agent configuration.

use_cases.title: Plan Large Feature Delivery
use_cases.description: Break a complex feature into agent roles, task queues, consensus checkpoints, and shared memory records.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Repository Review
use_cases.description: Assign focused review agents for code quality, security, tests, performance, and documentation.

use_cases.title: Run Structured Research
use_cases.description: Use research and analyst agents to compare options, vote on recommendations, and preserve decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Basic Hive
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a small project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the hive mind workflow to plan a small feature. Define the queen type, worker roles, first tasks, and status checks.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Consensus Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a hive mind plan for this architecture decision. Include worker assignments, voting method, evidence needed, and final approval criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Code Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a hive mind review for this pull request. Assign reviewers for security, tests, performance, docs, and release readiness.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a Multi-Hive Program
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a multi-hive coordination model for this program. Include shared memory, checkpoints, escalation rules, and performance metrics.

output_examples.input: Plan a hive mind workflow for building authentication.
output: Strategic queen owns scope, risk, and acceptance criteria.
Coder, tester, security, and documenter workers receive focused tasks.
Weighted consensus approves the implementation approach before coding starts.
Memory records store decisions, risks, and completed checkpoints.

output_examples.input: Review a pull request with hive mind coordination.
output: A tactical queen coordinates review order and response deadlines.
Specialist workers inspect security, performance, tests, and documentation.
Consensus decides whether to approve, request changes, or pause for clarification.

output_examples.input: Compare GraphQL and REST for a service migration.
output: Research agents gather project constraints and migration risks.
Analyst agents compare implementation cost, client needs, and operational impact.
The queen records the final recommendation and supporting evidence in shared memory.

best_practices: Choose the queen type before assigning workers, because it defines decision style and scope control.
Use consensus only for decisions that need traceability, review, or cross-role agreement.
Store decisions, assumptions, and unresolved risks in shared memory after each major checkpoint.
anti_patterns: Spawning many workers before the objective, roles, and acceptance criteria are clear.
Using Byzantine consensus for simple tasks that only need one owner.
Running documented CLI commands without checking the installed Claude Flow version and project context.

faq.question: What does this skill help coordinate?
faq.answer: It helps coordinate multi-agent software planning, implementation, review, research, and memory workflows.

faq.question: Does this skill execute commands by itself?
faq.answer: No. It documents workflows and command examples. Users or agents decide what to run.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: When should I use weighted consensus?
faq.answer: Use it when a queen coordinator should guide the result while still collecting worker votes.

faq.question: What is collective memory used for?
faq.answer: It stores decisions, context, task results, errors, metrics, and reusable knowledge across hive mind sessions.

faq.question: Is this best for beginners?
faq.answer: Beginners can use the basic workflows, but advanced features require comfort with CLI tools and agent coordination.
